title: No One is Righteous, Righteousness Through Faith

questions.question: Paul asks what advantage the Jew has, or what the value of circumcision is. He says "Much in every way." What is the first advantage he lists?
options: The Jews were entrusted with the oracles of God
To them belong the adoption, the glory, the covenants
From their race, according to the flesh, is the Christ
They received the law through angels directly from God
questions.correctAnswer: The Jews were entrusted with the oracles of God
questions.explanation: Romans 3:1-2 (ESV): "Then what advantage has the Jew? Or what is the value of circumcision? Much in every way. To begin with, the Jews were entrusted with the oracles of God."

questions.question: If some were unfaithful, does their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? Paul says: "By no means! Let God be true though every one were a ____."
options: liar
sinner
hypocrite
lawbreaker
questions.explanation: Romans 3:3-4 (ESV): "What if some were unfaithful? Does their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? By no means! Let God be true though every one were a liar,"

questions.question: If our unrighteousness serves to show the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous to inflict wrath on us? Paul says by no means, because otherwise...
options: How could God judge the world?
How would he maintain his holiness?
How could there be any salvation?
How would the law be fulfilled?
questions.correctAnswer: How could God judge the world?
questions.explanation: Romans 3:5-6 (ESV): "...Is God unrighteous to inflict wrath on us? (I speak in a human way.) By no means! For then how could God judge the world?"

questions.question: Some people were reportedly slandering Paul by claiming he taught a false doctrine. What was the false teaching they accused him of?
options: "Let us do evil that good may come."
"Let us sin that grace may abound."
"Let us ignore the law for we are free."
"Let us abandon Moses and trust only in Christ."
questions.correctAnswer: "Let us do evil that good may come."
questions.explanation: Romans 3:8 (ESV): "And why not do evil that good may come?—as some people slanderously charge us with saying. Their condemnation is just."

questions.question: Are Jews any better off than Gentiles under sin? What does Paul conclude after charging that all, both Jews and Greeks, are under sin?
options: "None is righteous, no, not one;"
"All have stumbled, the Jew and the Greek alike,"
"There is no difference in the flesh, only in the spirit,"
"Jew and Gentile are both captive to the same dark master,"
questions.explanation: Romans 3:9-10 (ESV): "For we have already charged that all, both Jews and Greeks, are under sin, as it is written: 'None is righteous, no, not one;'"

questions.question: In the string of Old Testament quotes in verses 10-18 painting a grim picture of human sinfulness, what is said about their throats?
options: "Their throat is an open grave"
"Their throat utters lies continuously"
"Their throat is full of bitterness and cursing"
"Their throat devours the poor and needy"
questions.explanation: Romans 3:13 (ESV): "Their throat is an open grave; they use their tongues to deceive."

questions.question: What is the final characteristic of humanity described in the string of quotes from the Psalms and Isaiah in verse 18?
options: "There is no fear of God before their eyes."
"They do not know the way of peace."
"Their feet are swift to shed blood."
"There is no one who does good."
questions.correctAnswer: "There is no fear of God before their eyes."
questions.explanation: Romans 3:18 (ESV): "There is no fear of God before their eyes."

questions.question: Whatever the law says it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped, and the whole world may be held ____.
options: accountable to God
guilty before the throne
under the wrath of the Almighty
captive to sin
questions.explanation: Romans 3:19 (ESV): "Now we know that whatever the law says it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped, and the whole world may be held accountable to God."

questions.question: Paul concludes that by works of the law no human being will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes what?
options: Knowledge of sin
The power of sin
The curse of disobedience
Condemnation for all
questions.explanation: Romans 3:20 (ESV): "For by works of the law no human being will be justified in his sight, since through the law comes knowledge of sin."

questions.question: But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although what bear witness to it?
options: The Law and the Prophets
The heavens and the earth
The Spirit and the water
The apostles and the early saints
questions.explanation: Romans 3:21 (ESV): "But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it—"

questions.question: This righteousness of God is through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. Why is there no distinction?
options: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God
Because God loves the world equally in Christ
For both Jew and Gentile share the same human nature
Because the law was given that all might seek grace
questions.correctAnswer: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God
questions.explanation: Romans 3:22-23 (ESV): "For there is no distinction: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,"

questions.question: They are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a ____ by his blood, to be received by faith.
options: propitiation
sacrifice of atonement
ransom payment
mercy seat
questions.explanation: Romans 3:24-25 (ESV): "and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith."

questions.question: Why did God put forward Christ as a propitiation to show God's righteousness?
options: Because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins
Because the blood of bulls and goats could not take away sins
To satisfy the demands of the law that required blood
To demonstrate his love for the world in a tangible way
questions.correctAnswer: Because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins
questions.explanation: Romans 3:25 (ESV): "This was to show God's righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins."

questions.question: What happens to boasting, since a person is justified by faith apart from works of the law?
options: It is excluded
It is redirected to God
It is made void
It is shifted from works to faith
questions.explanation: Romans 3:27 (ESV): "Then what becomes of our boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith."

questions.question: Do we then overthrow the law by this faith? Paul answers: "By no means! On the contrary, we ____ the law."
options: uphold
fulfill
establish
complete
questions.explanation: Romans 3:31 (ESV): "Do we then overthrow the law by this faith? By no means! On the contrary, we uphold the law."

key_verse_text: For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
